The game is good. Very complicated. Lots of research outside of the game is necessary to understand it, which is great if you are the inquisitive sort. 

The developers have done a great job at adding new content. There has been a consistent update schedule over the past several years, with major story updates in the winter/ summer, and slightly smaller updates during spring/ fall. 

The updates in question are quite predictable. Each major story update can be summed up as a content island. There is a hub with NPCs that can be befriended and the NPCs offer weapons, upgrades, parts for a new character, or decorations. The story progresses by befriending the NPCs. Each hub is generally unrelated to previous and future ones, so once you collect everything from one, there is little reason to return. 

Given the seasonal update nature of the game, the narrative progresses incredibly slow. The devs have therefore written a story that is intentionally cryptic to encourage discussion and speculation in between updates to keep people entertained. It works, because players are still arguing over the concept of eternalism since its introduction nearly four years ago.

I have never had a free to play game with this much content and support.  New updates are always rolling out to keep things fresh and exciting.  I would write more but the awesomeness of this game speaks for itself.

10/16/2017
I have been playing this game for several years now and feel over this time that I have grown as a gamer.  In light of that revelation I felt that I should return to some of my previous reviews and update  them.  Even though I put Warframe down from time to time, it always draws me back in.  I stand by my origional statement that this games development team is more dedicated to keeping this game fun and fresh.  They have just recently dropped a new expansion called The Plains of Eidolon.  This new area is an open world environment for old and new players to explore.  The base area itself is fairly low level so new players aren't jumping into a nightmare zone.  You can adjust the level of the area by taking out high level bounties from quest givers in the city of Cetus.  Cetus acts as a hub, much like the Relays, for players to get missions and turn in rep for rewards from the new factions.  It is not nessecary to take missions or bounties to enjoy The Plains.  You can simply bypass Cetus and jump straight into the base Plains.  Random missions spawn up around you all of the time, which often lead to Lotus bugging you but what else is new.  You can do many thungs on The Plains like fishing, harvesting gems, exploring caves, or just killing the Grineer.  The graphics for this new 'tile set' are far more amazing than anything the Dev's have produced before.  The water and lighting effects are as crisp and natural as you would expect from a AAA publisher.  The overal detail in the terran is complemented by the natural wildlife and the insanity of the occupying Grineer forces.  The transition from day to night and night to day is amazingly well done.  At first I was skeptical about this expansion because it felt very grindy and was rather difficult.  However, after rallying the members of my dojo together, I found that it didn't have to be about grinding rep with the new factions (plus there is a limit to the amount of rep you can get from turning in stuff).  There is plenty to do either solo or in a group on The Plains of Eidolon.  I rate this expansion a 9/10 until the bugs have been worked out (it has been out less than a week at the time of this review).  The overall game itself has always been one that I will be playing for years to come.

11/26/2018
The Fortuna update is another masterpiece by the developers of this game.  I have never enjoyed a free to play game as much as this one.

100 hours later, and i still have no idea of what i'm doing.

but it is Fun.

This game is the model free2play game if I had to pick one. All updates and DLC types introductions such as new weapons, Warframes (In game suits), and pets can all be obtained by playing the game. Unlike other free to plays where there are some premium items or getting said items requires you to dedicate all you time to just that one thing for 12 hours a day to get that get a single upgrade.
  
 I myself am a founder and have played well over two thousand hours worth of game time not including per wipe. Anyone who enjoys third person shooters and doesn't want to spend money needs to get this game. Along with the new parkour update its just an amazing experience overall.

The Developers Digital Extreme are always adding new guns and swords with more frames and pets. Making there always something worth getting and keep coming back.

I burnt out hard on Warframe just over a year ago, mainly due to playing almost excluively on my own or with randoms while having matchmaking set to public. 
Now I've started playing with friends and they game is infinitely more enjoyable.
